post.caption:
38 minutes for your laundry. 0 for your heart. 🧺

Sunday, 11:20 p.m. Machine number 4. The shirt you wore at dinner — and what you said to your brother — still on you. A woman folds her clothes, whispering “astaghfirullah” with every fold. Your shirt will come out clean. You won’t.

“Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver.” (71:10)

This evening at Maghrib: one apology. Then 100 “Astaghfirullah.”

captions: Sunday, 11:20 p.m. Machine number 4. The drum turns.
That shirt. The one you wore at dinner tonight.
What you said to your brother. It’s still on you.
You scroll. You check the timer. 23 minutes left.
The light flickers. A woman folds her clothes, whispering.
Your shirt will come out clean. You won’t.
Next day. Maghrib. Your balcony, the tea going cold.
Your brother’s number. You call. “I’m sorry.”
The sun goes down. And something in you comes clean.

verses.text: “Ask forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in [continuing] showers.”
